expectations.text: The plan records the 3D source (three-scene, generated-image, css-depth or mesh-generator) and why
expectations.evidence: No plan artifact exists: mech.json plan: [null, 'no site-plan.json'], and the only non-site file under /tmp/create-website/workspace/iteration-1/portfolio-with-3d-hero/without_skill/outputs/ is REPORT.md plus tools/gen-assets.mjs. REPORT.md describes what was built ('A faceted brass core inside a glass shell, inside a wire cage... three.js r0.169.0, exact pinned version, ES module from cdn.jsdelivr.net') but never records a choice among sources with a reason. The nearest thing is assumption 6, 'Had generation been available, the brief would have been: nothing. Photographic hero imagery would have fought the 3D object' — a reason for declining generated imagery, written after the build, not a recorded source decision.

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, the code checks availability and shows a still fallback when it is missing
expectations.evidence: Half of it holds. Availability is checked, loosely, by construction in a try/catch — site/assets/js/hero.js lines 17-28: `try { renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({...}); } catch (err) { canvas.remove(); return; }`. But there is no still. The file's own header comment says what happens instead: 'Falls back silently to the CSS gradient behind the canvas if WebGL or the module is unavailable.' REPORT.md repeats it: 'the stage carries a CSS gradient behind the canvas, so a failed WebGL context, a blocked CDN or JS off leaves a composed dark hero with the headline intact.' site/index.html lines 34-46 confirm `.hero__stage` holds only `` and `.hero__copy` — no ``, and no hero still exists in site/assets/img/ (the six SVGs there are case-study plates). A reader with no WebGL gets a gradient where the subject of the page should be.

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, setPixelRatio is capped at 2 or lower
expectations.evidence: site/assets/js/hero.js line 30 and again in the resize path at line 138: `renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2));`. Both call sites are capped. mech.json dpr_capped: true. REPORT.md also measures the result: 'canvas.width = 2880 at DPR 2'.

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, rendering pauses when the canvas is off-screen or the tab is hidden
expectations.evidence: The off-screen half is implemented, which is what the assertion's 'or' requires. site/assets/js/hero.js lines 187-192: `let visible = true; new IntersectionObserver((entries) => { visible = entries[0].isIntersecting; dirty = true; }, { rootMargin: "120px" }).observe(hero);` and the frame loop at line 198 begins `requestAnimationFrame(frame); if (!visible) return;`. mech.json offscreen_pause: true. Noting for accuracy: there is no `visibilitychange` handler, so the hidden-tab case relies on the browser throttling requestAnimationFrame rather than on the page.

expectations.text: If a WebGL canvas is created, a webglcontextlost handler shows the still
expectations.evidence: No such handler exists. `grep -n 'contextlost|contextrestored' site/assets/js/hero.js` returns nothing, and the string appears nowhere in site/assets/js/. mech.json contextlost: false. A lost context therefore leaves a frozen or blank canvas with no recovery and no still to fall back to — and as above, the page ships no still at all.

expectations.text: The canvas is aria-hidden or named, with any controls in HTML
expectations.evidence: site/index.html line 36: `<canvas id="hero-canvas" aria-hidden="true"></canvas>`. All hero content is HTML beside it, lines 38-45: the `<h1 class="hero__title" id="hero-title">`, the subheading and the three `hero__meta` spans. The second clause is vacuous here — the run creates no canvas controls of any kind (no turn buttons, no keyboard affordance), so the rotation is reachable only by scrolling or a pointer drag.

expectations.text: Under prefers-reduced-motion the 3D rotation and scroll effects stop and all content is visible
expectations.evidence: Content is visible — site/assets/css/main.css lines 394-396, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .js [data-reveal] { opacity: 1; transform: none; transition: none; } }` — but the 3D rotation does not stop. In site/assets/js/hero.js, `reduced` only zeroes the idle drift and skips redundant frames: line 210 `const idle = reduced ? 0 : t * 0.055;` and line 207 `if (!moving && !dirty && reduced) return;  // fully static under reduced motion`. The scroll driver is untouched: `progress` is still written by the scroll listener (line 160 `progress = p;`, line 173 `window.addEventListener("scroll", readProgress, { passive: true })`), and lines 212-219 still apply it — `rig.rotation.y = shown * Math.PI * 2.3 + idle; rig.rotation.x = Math.sin(shown * Math.PI) * 0.62 + py * 0.12; core.rotation.y = -shown * Math.PI * 1.1;` and four more. So a reduced-motion visitor scrolling the page still gets just over two full revolutions of a five-part counter-rotating object. The comment 'fully static under reduced motion' is accurate only while the visitor is not scrolling, and the run's own check recorded the weaker claim: REPORT.md, 'Reduced motion ... Reveals bypassed, hero still renders, idle rotation off'.

expectations.text: No wheel or touchmove preventDefault and no normalizeScroll is used
expectations.evidence: `grep -rn 'normalizeScroll|preventDefault|wheel|touchmove' site/assets/js/ site/*.html` returns no matches at all. Scroll and pointer listeners are registered passive (`window.addEventListener("scroll", readProgress, { passive: true })`, line 173; pointermove at line 180-184 likewise). Native scrolling is intact. mech.json wheel_preventDefault_or_normalize: false.

expectations.text: Case-study metrics, clients or quotes that the prompt did not supply are marked as gaps, not invented
expectations.evidence: The pages are full of invented figures presented as results. case-banking-app.html meta description: 'Mistaken-payment reports fell 34% in the pilot cohort.' case-hospital-wayfinding.html: 'Questions at the main reception desk fell 41%.' case-bike-share-kiosk.html: 'Median unassisted hire fell from 2m 10s to 38s.' A scan for percentages returns 34%, 41%, 44%, 61%, 12%, 22%, 6%, 71%, 60%, 58%, 17%, 19% across the three case pages and the home page, none supplied by the prompt. The identity is fabricated too: 'the site is written for a fictional designer — *Maren Avelo*, Lisbon, studio@marenavelo.example', shipped on the page as 'Based in Lisbon' and 'Available Q2 2027'. The run states the problem plainly in REPORT.md assumption 2 — '**Case-study content is invented.** Metrics (-34%, -41%, 38s), team shapes, durations and quotes are plausible fabrications... they are not real results' — but the assertion asks for them to be marked as gaps rather than invented, and on the page there is no marker: a reader sees '34%', not a placeholder.

expectations.text: The no-WebGL capture pass shows the fallback and reports no uncaught exception
expectations.evidence: No no-WebGL pass was run and no capture artifact exists: mech.json capture: {'pngs': 0}, and no PNG or capture report is present anywhere under outputs/. REPORT.md's check table lists 'Hero actually renders', 'Rotation is scroll-driven', 'JS errors', 'Reduced motion' and others, but nothing that disables WebGL; its 'Not checked' section names 'Real iOS/Android devices, Safari and Firefox... and sustained frame rate under load' and does not mention the no-WebGL path either. The fallback claim in REPORT.md ('a failed WebGL context... leaves a composed dark hero with the headline intact') is asserted, never exercised.

claims.claim: Under prefers-reduced-motion idle drift is off and frames are only drawn when the user actually scrolls
claims.evidence: Literally true of the code (idle = 0, redundant frames skipped) — but it concedes that frames ARE drawn when the user scrolls, which is the behaviour the reduced-motion assertion rules out. The claim is accurate and the design it describes is the defect.

claims.claim: The hero never initialised because of a temporal dead zone throw, found and fixed during the checks
claims.evidence: Consistent with the shipped file: in hero.js the state declarations (`let dirty`, `let visible`) now sit above their use. The fix is in the code; the discovery narrative itself rests on the run's summary, as no console artifact was retained.

claims.claim: Contrast: body 17.3:1, muted 7.9:1, brass 8.9:1, all computed from source hex
claims.evidence: Reported as prose with no measurement artifact. The related fix is visible — `--fg-dim` is no longer #6d7684 — but the ratios cannot be checked from what was kept.

claims.claim: Metrics on the case studies are fabrications and replacing them is the first editing pass
claims.evidence: REPORT.md assumption 2 states it; the pages ship the numbers unmarked, so the disclosure lives only in a file the site's reader never sees.

hero.js line 8: `import * as THREE from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.169.0/build/three.module.js";` — a runtime third-party request, and one more path on which the hero silently becomes a gradient.

assertions_that_could_not_fail_or_both_a: 'No wheel or touchmove preventDefault and no normalizeScroll is used' — both arms pass. Neither attempted a scroll-hijacking library, so there was nothing for this to catch.
'If a WebGL canvas is created, setPixelRatio is capped at 2 or lower' — both arms pass with the same standard three.js one-liner; it is close to a free pass.

'The canvas is aria-hidden or named, with any controls in HTML' — both arms pass, and for this arm the second clause cannot fail: it builds no canvas controls at all, so 'any controls in HTML' is satisfied by their absence. A run that makes the rotation reachable only by scroll scores the same as one that ships labelled turn buttons.
other_observations: The reduced-motion assertion is the sharpest one in this eval: it caught a defect that the run's own check passed ('idle rotation off') because the check tested the idle animation and not the scroll driver.

No assertion covers whether the hero's 3D dependency is loaded from a third party at runtime, which this arm does. A blocked or slow CDN drops the page's entire subject with no still behind it, and nothing in the eval sees that.
